name: Amazon API Gateway
oneLiner: REST and HTTP bill per request. WebSocket bills per message and per minute a socket stays open.
trap: HTTP API requests meter in 512KB increments and WebSocket messages in 32KB, so one fat payload becomes several billed units. Connection minutes accrue on idle sockets carrying no traffic at all.

name: AWS AppFlow
oneLiner: A flat charge per flow run, plus per GB moved. Schedule frequency is what drives the total.
trap: Cost follows cadence rather than data size for most flows: a one-minute schedule is roughly 43,000 runs a month. Data landing at a destination outside AWS is charged at a higher per-GB rate.

name: AWS AppSync
oneLiner: Three meters: per GraphQL operation, per real-time update pushed, and per minute a client stays subscribed.
trap: Real-time updates meter per 5KB of payload, so an 8KB push bills as two messages. Connection minutes tick while a subscriber sits idle and are entirely independent of how many updates you send.

name: Amazon Chime SDK
oneLiner: Attendee-minutes and messages dominate; phone numbers rent monthly.
trap: The Amazon Chime application hit end of support in February 2026. That did not touch the Chime SDK, which bills as normal. Separately, each provisioned DID costs a monthly rental at zero call volume.

name: Amazon Connect
oneLiner: Per-minute and per-message usage, plus a daily rent on every claimed phone number.
trap: People budget the per-minute voice rate and forget the number itself. A claimed DID or toll-free number accrues a daily charge until you release it back to inventory, even if nobody ever dials it.

name: Amazon Data Firehose
oneLiner: Billed on bytes ingested rather than bytes delivered, with no shards to provision.
trap: Direct PUT rounds each record up to the next 5KB multiple, so a 12KB record bills as 15KB and a million 1KB records bill as 5GB. MSK and vended logs as sources skip the rounding entirely.

name: Amazon EventBridge
oneLiner: Custom and partner events bill on ingestion. AWS service events land on the default bus for free.
trap: A 200KB event is four billed events because each 64KB chunk counts as one, and Schema Discovery slices at 8KB. API destinations, Pipes and Scheduler invocations each carry their own per-million rate.

name: AWS IoT Core
oneLiner: Messages meter in 5 KB blocks; connection minutes tick on their own.
trap: An 8 KB publish bills as two messages and a 200 byte publish as one, so padding toward 5 KB is free but spilling past it is not. A triggered rule always meters at least one rule and one action, even if no action fires.

name: AWS IoT Device Management
oneLiner: Every fleet operation is a countable unit.
trap: Fleet indexing meters index updates in 1 KB chunks, so one fat shadow document reindexes as several updates each time it changes. Jobs bill per remote action delivered to a device, which multiplies across a large fleet.

name: AWS IoT Events
oneLiner: Gone. Full shutdown on 20 May 2026; new customers were blocked a year earlier.
trap: Not merely deprecated: AWS lists it under full shutdown, so it is gone from the portfolio and its pricing page redirects. While it ran, alarms billed monthly and messages per evaluation.

name: AWS IoT Greengrass
oneLiner: A core device that authenticates once in a month bills for that whole month.
trap: Only the core is metered. Devices talking to it over the local network cost nothing, but everything the core relays upward lands on IoT Core connection, messaging and shadow meters, which usually dwarf the per-core fee.

name: AWS IoT SiteWise
oneLiner: All three shapes at once: per-message ingest, GB-hour storage tiers, per-GB scanned on every query.
trap: ExecuteQuery bills by GB scanned, so a wide time window over a busy asset model can cost more than the ingest that produced the data. Hot tier storage meters by GB-hour and keeps running after the devices go quiet.

name: AWS IoT TwinMaker
oneLiner: Entities carry a monthly fee even when nobody opens the twin.
trap: Entity count is the sticky line. Model a plant at fine granularity and you create thousands of entities that bill every month, while queries and unified data access calls only bill when someone actually reads.

name: Amazon Kinesis Data Streams
oneLiner: Provisioned charges shard-hours plus 25KB PUT payload units. On-demand charges a stream-hour plus GB in and out.
trap: The two modes meter differently. Provisioned rounds each record up to a 25KB payload unit, so a 1KB record is a full unit. On-demand charges per GB written, so ingress is not free here.

name: Amazon Location Service
oneLiner: Per thousand requests across maps, places and routes, with stored geofences ticking monthly.
trap: A route matrix bills origins multiplied by destinations, so one call with 10 origins and 10 destinations is 100 routes. Asking for results you may store moves you onto a separate usage type costing several times more.

name: Amazon MQ
oneLiner: Broker hours and storage, nothing per message.
trap: No per-message or per-API charge exists in either engine, so throughput barely moves the bill. Active/standby doubles the instance hours and a three-node RabbitMQ cluster triples them.

name: Amazon Managed Streaming for Apache Kafka
oneLiner: Kafka brokers by the hour plus storage. Serverless swaps that for cluster-hours and partition-hours.
trap: Neither mode charges per message or per API call. Serverless bills every partition every hour, so an over-partitioned idle topic costs real money, and Express brokers add a per-GB-written fee.

name: Amazon Pinpoint
oneLiner: Per endpoint targeted each month, plus per message on whichever channel does the sending.
trap: Monthly Targeted Audience counts every endpoint a campaign or journey touches, deliverable or not. Support ends 30 October 2026; SMS, voice, push and OTP move to AWS End User Messaging.

name: Amazon SES
oneLiner: Outbound meters per recipient. One send to fifty addresses is fifty charges.
trap: Attachment bytes bill per GB on top of the recipient count. Receiving bills per email and again per 256KB chunk, so one big attachment hits twice. Pro and Enterprise plans add a fixed monthly fee.

name: Amazon SNS
oneLiner: Publishing costs money. So does delivery, but only to certain endpoint types.
trap: SQS and Lambda deliveries are free. HTTP/S, mobile push and Firehose all bill per notification, and email is the priciest of the lot by a wide margin. SMS bills through AWS End User Messaging.

name: Amazon SQS
oneLiner: Every API action counts as a request. Sends, receives, deletes and empty polls all bill the same.
trap: A ReceiveMessage that returns nothing still bills, and payload chunks: a 1 MiB call bills as sixteen requests. Standard queue calls carrying a message group ID are charged fair-queue rates on top.

name: AWS Step Functions
oneLiner: Standard bills per state transition. Express swaps that for a per-start charge plus memory-seconds.
trap: Standard counts every transition, retries included. Distributed Map bills one per iteration, an Inline Map none — so not every loop costs. Express bills duration times memory instead.

name: Amazon WorkMail
oneLiner: Flat per-mailbox monthly seat, prorated by the hour.
trap: Billing tracks active user accounts, not logins. Deactivating a user mid-month earns no credit for the remaining days, and the 50 GB per user is bundled, so there is no separate storage meter.
